conversation.content: I want to build a website for my business.
What type of business is this for, and what's the main goal you want the website to achieve (e.g., generate leads, sell products online, provide information, book appointments)?

It's a local service business — we do home renovation and remodeling work. Honestly, I need the website to do a few things: show our portfolio of past projects so people can see what we're capable of, make it easy for potential customers to contact us, and ideally get more leads coming in from the area.

When someone wants to reach out, what would you like them to do — fill out a contact/quote request form, call directly, or something like scheduling a consultation? And what key details do you want to capture from them (e.g., project type, budget, photos of their space)?

I think a contact form would be best — I'd rather have it in writing so I can review the details before following up. For the form, I'd want to know what type of project they're interested in, their general timeline, and ideally some idea of budget so I'm not wasting time on stuff we can't do. A phone number so we can reach them, obviously, and maybe an option for them to upload photos of their space if they want to.

Got it. For the portfolio section, do you want to be able to add/update past projects yourself over time (needing a simple admin/CMS), or is it fine to have a developer update it for you whenever you complete a new project?

I'd prefer to be able to update it myself — I don't want to have to contact a developer every time we finish a job. Plus, I'd like to add new projects pretty quickly while they're fresh. As long as it's not too complicated, I can handle it.
What geographic area(s) do you serve (city/region), and do you have existing branding materials ready to go — like a logo, brand colors, and professional photos of past projects?

We serve the greater metro area — probably about a 20-30 mile radius from our main office. As for branding, we have a logo that we've been using for a few years, and I can give you the colors we typically use. For photos, we have some decent ones from past projects on our phones and old emails, but they're kind of all over the place — some are pretty good quality, others not so much.
Do you have a target timeline for launching the site, and a rough budget range you're working with for this project?

I'd like to have it live within the next couple months if possible — we're trying to pick up more business before the busy season hits. As for budget, I'm not totally sure what's realistic, but I'm thinking somewhere in the $3,000 to $8,000 range? I know that might be low, but I want to make sure it's worth the investment before we go crazy with it.
Last question: do you already own a domain name and have hosting set up, or would you need help securing/setting those up as part of this project?
I don't have either yet. I've got a domain name in mind, but I haven't purchased it. So yeah, I'd need help getting that all set up — I'm not really sure how all that works to be honest.

[DONE]

**Summary of Requirements Gathered:**

- **Business type:** Local home renovation/remodeling company
- **Website goals:** Showcase portfolio, generate leads, make contact easy
- **Lead capture:** Contact form (not live chat/phone-first) collecting:
  - Project type
  - Timeline
  - Budget range
  - Phone number
  - Optional photo upload of their space
- **Portfolio management:** Needs self-service CMS/admin panel to add/update projects without developer help
- **Service area:** Greater metro area, ~20-30 mile radius from main office
- **Branding assets:** Existing logo and brand colors available; photos are mixed quality, scattered across phone/email
- **Timeline:** Launch within ~2 months (before busy season)
- **Budget:** $3,000–$8,000
- **Domain/Hosting:** No domain purchased yet (has one in mind), no hosting set up — needs full assistance with setup
I need an app that helps people manage their tasks.
Who is the primary audience for this task management app — individuals managing personal to-dos, or teams collaborating on shared work?

Honestly, I'm thinking primarily about individuals right now — people like me who just want a better way to organize personal tasks and maybe work projects. But I could see teams finding it useful too if we built in some collaboration features. I haven't thought super deeply about team needs yet, but personal task management is definitely where I'm starting.
Got it — focusing on individual users first, with room to expand to team features later. What platform(s) do you want to launch on first: mobile (iOS/Android), web, desktop, or some combination?

I think web first makes the most sense — that seems like the easiest way to get something out there quickly. But honestly, I'd want it on my phone too eventually since a lot of my tasks come up when I'm out and about. Mobile is probably more important than desktop for me personally.
What are the must-have core features for organizing tasks — things like due dates, reminders/notifications, categories or projects, priority levels, recurring tasks, or subtasks?

Due dates and maybe some way to organize tasks into categories or projects are definitely essential. Priority levels would be helpful too so I can focus on what actually matters. Reminders would be nice but not a dealbreaker for launch. Recurring tasks and subtasks feel more like nice-to-haves down the road — I don't think I need those to start.

Since you'll eventually want this synced between web and mobile, do you need user accounts with login (email/password, Google sign-in, etc.) so tasks sync across devices, or is a simpler local-only setup okay for now?

Yeah, I'd definitely need user accounts and syncing across devices — otherwise what's the point of having both web and mobile? I don't really care how the login works, whether it's email or Google sign-in or whatever, as long as my tasks are there when I switch between devices.
Makes sense. Do you have a rough budget or timeline in mind for building this first version (the web app with accounts, sync, and core task features)?

I haven't really nailed down exact numbers, but I'm hoping to keep costs reasonable — maybe a few thousand dollars? As for timeline, I'd like to get something usable out within a few months, but I'm flexible if it takes longer. I'm more focused on getting it right than hitting a specific date.
One last question: do you have any preference for visual style or existing apps whose design/UX you admire (e.g., clean and minimal like Todoist, or something else), to guide the look and feel?

I like clean and simple — nothing too cluttered. I've used Todoist before and their interface is pretty straightforward, which I appreciate. I don't need anything fancy or colorful, just something intuitive where I can quickly add and check off tasks without getting lost in menus.

[DONE]

**Summary of Requirements Gathered:**

- **Target Users:** Individuals managing personal tasks and work projects (team collaboration features possible in future, not initial priority)
- **Platforms:** Web app first (MVP), followed by mobile app (iOS/Android) — desktop not a priority
- **Core Features (Must-Have for Launch):**
  - Due dates
  - Categories/projects for organization
  - Priority levels
- **Nice-to-Have (Future):**
  - Reminders/notifications
  - Recurring tasks
  - Subtasks
- **Accounts & Sync:** User authentication required (method flexible — email/password, Google sign-in, etc.) with cross-device sync between web and mobile
- **Budget:** Approximately a few thousand dollars
- **Timeline:** Flexible, aiming for a usable version within a few months; prioritizing quality over speed
- **Design/UX Preference:** Clean, minimal, intuitive interface similar to Todoist — quick task entry and completion without clutter or complex menus
I want to sell products online.
What kind of products will you be selling (physical goods, digital downloads, subscriptions, or a mix), and roughly how many products/SKUs do you expect to list initially?

I'm thinking physical goods to start with — probably clothing and accessories. As for volume, I'm planning to launch with maybe 50 to 100 products initially, though I might expand from there depending on how it goes.

Great, that gives a clear starting point. Do you already have a preferred platform or approach in mind — for example, using an existing solution like Shopify/WooCommerce, or building a fully custom online store from scratch?

Honestly, I haven't decided yet. I've heard good things about Shopify because it seems pretty straightforward, but I'm open to other options if there's something better. I don't think I need a fully custom build right away — I just want to get up and running without spending a fortune.

That's helpful — Shopify or a similar hosted platform sounds like a good fit for your needs. What's your budget range for getting this store built and launched, and do you have a target launch date in mind?

I'm looking to keep it under $5,000 to get started, ideally closer to $2,000-$3,000 if possible. As for timeline, I'd like to launch within the next couple of months — I know there's no time to waste in getting this off the ground.
Good to know. For payments and shipping, do you need to sell/ship only within your home country to start, or are you planning to offer international shipping as well?

I'll start with just my home country to keep things simple. International shipping seems complicated with customs and all that, so I'd rather nail the basics first and maybe expand internationally down the road if things go well.
Do you already have branding assets ready — like a logo, brand colors/style guide, and product photography — or will those need to be created as part of this project?

I don't have much yet, honestly. I've got a rough idea of what I want the brand to look like, but I don't have a logo or professional product photos. I'll definitely need help with photography and probably getting a logo designed, but I'm hoping to keep those costs reasonable.

Last question: will you be managing the store operations yourself (inventory, order fulfillment, customer service), or do you need this built in a way that someone else on your team can easily run it day-to-day?

I'll be managing it myself for now — at least initially. So I need something that's fairly straightforward for one person to handle, but it doesn't need to be overly complex or built for a big team right away.

[DONE]

**Summary of Requirements Gathered:**

- **Product type:** Physical goods — clothing and accessories
- **Initial catalog size:** 50–100 SKUs, with potential to expand
- **Platform preference:** Leaning toward Shopify or similar hosted e-commerce solution (no custom build needed)
- **Budget:** Under $5,000, ideally $2,000–$3,000
- **Timeline:** Launch within the next couple of months
- **Shipping/Market scope:** Domestic only to start; international expansion considered for later
- **Branding needs:** No existing logo, brand guide, or product photography — will need cost-effective design and photography help
- **Operations:** Single-person management (solo founder), so the store setup should be simple and not overly complex for day-to-day running (inventory, fulfillment, customer service)
Help me do marketing for my startup.
What does your startup do, and what product or service are you marketing?

We're building a SaaS platform for small e-commerce businesses to automate their inventory management. Right now we're still pretty early — we have an MVP and a handful of beta users — so we need help getting the word out and figuring out our go-to-market strategy.
What's your primary goal for this marketing push right now — for example, a specific number of new signups/customers, raising a funding round, or building brand awareness?

Honestly, our main goal right now is just to get more traction and validate that there's real demand for what we're building. We'd love to hit maybe 50-100 paying customers in the next few months so we can prove the model works and have some revenue to show. That would also help us when we go to pitch investors down the line.
What's your marketing budget for the next few months, and do you have any dedicated marketing team members, or is this mostly you (and maybe co-founders) handling it alongside product work?

We've got maybe $5,000-10,000 we can spend on marketing over the next few months, but honestly that's being pretty generous with ourselves. Right now it's mostly me handling marketing along with my co-founder who's focused on product — we don't have a dedicated marketing person. So we're looking for strategies that don't require a huge budget or a ton of time commitment.

Can you tell me more about your ideal customer — what specific type of small e-commerce business (e.g., platform used like Shopify, product category, order volume) gets the most value from your inventory automation, and where do you currently find or interact with your beta users?

Our sweet spot is really Shopify stores doing between $50k-$500k in annual revenue — they're big enough that manual inventory management is a real pain, but small enough that they can't afford enterprise solutions. We've found our beta users mostly through direct outreach in Shopify communities and Facebook groups for e-commerce sellers, plus a couple came through our networks. We haven't done much paid advertising yet. Most of them seem to sell either apparel or general retail products where tracking stock across multiple channels is actually critical.

What makes your solution different from other inventory management tools Shopify merchants might already know about (like existing apps in the Shopify App Store), and do you have a clear pricing model in place yet?

We're focused on simplicity and affordability — a lot of existing tools are overly complex and charge $200+ per month, which is way too much for smaller stores. We're building something specifically designed for the Shopify workflow and keeping it dead simple to set up, no coding required. As for pricing, we're still testing it with our beta users, but we're thinking around $29-49 per month depending on the plan, which is way more accessible.
One last question: what's your target timeline to hit that 50-100 paying customer goal — are you thinking 3 months, 6 months, or something else?

We're hoping to get there in the next 3-4 months, but I'll be honest — that might be optimistic depending on how quickly we can get word out and iterate based on feedback. If we can nail down our messaging and find the right channels to reach these store owners, I think it's doable. But we're trying to be realistic too.

[DONE]

**Summary of gathered requirements:**

- **Product:** SaaS platform automating inventory management for small e-commerce businesses (Shopify-focused)
- **Stage:** Early — MVP built, small group of beta users, no paid advertising yet
- **Primary goal:** Acquire 50-100 paying customers in 3-4 months to validate demand and support future investor pitches
- **Budget:** $5,000-$10,000 total for the next few months (lean/bootstrapped)
- **Team/resources:** Founder handling marketing part-time; co-founder focused on product; no dedicated marketing hire
- **Target customer:** Shopify stores with $50k-$500k annual revenue, primarily apparel/general retail sellers with multi-channel stock tracking needs
- **Current channels:** Direct outreach in Shopify communities, Facebook groups for e-commerce sellers, personal network referrals
- **Competitive positioning:** Simpler and more affordable than existing tools (which often run $200+/month); no-code, easy setup tailored to Shopify workflow
- **Pricing:** Still being tested, targeting $29-49/month tiered plans
- **Timeline:** 3-4 months to reach customer goal, acknowledged as ambitious
I want a website and some way to get more customers.
What type of business or service is this website for, and who is your target customer?

We're a local home cleaning service, and we mainly want to reach homeowners in our area who are too busy to clean their own homes or just prefer to outsource it. Right now we're mostly getting customers through word-of-mouth and neighborhood Facebook groups, but we need a better way to get our name out there.
What's the main action you want visitors to take on your website—request a quote, book a cleaning directly online, call you, or something else?

I think we'd want people to be able to request a quote or at least contact us easily—maybe fill out a form with details about their home and what they need cleaned, and then we can follow up with them. Ideally we'd also want a phone number they can call, but starting with the form would help us manage inquiries better than we do now.
Do you already have branding elements like a logo, colors, or photos of your team/work, or would those need to be created as part of this project?

We have a basic logo and some colors we've been using on our Facebook page, so you can work with that. We also have a bunch of photos on our phones from cleaning jobs we've done—some before and afters that customers loved. We might need help organizing those and taking some new professional photos, but we've got material to work with.

Beyond the website itself, what did you have in mind for actually driving traffic and new customers to it—things like local SEO/Google Business optimization, paid social/Google ads, email marketing, or something else?

Honestly, I'm not totally sure what all the options are, but I know people search for "cleaning service near me" on Google all the time. So getting found there would be huge for us. Maybe we could also run some ads on Facebook or Instagram since that's where we're already active a little bit. I don't really have experience with email marketing, so I'm not sure if that makes sense for us right now.
What's your budget range and timeline for getting this website and marketing effort up and running?

We're probably looking to spend somewhere between $2,000 and $5,000 total if possible—we want it done right but we're still a smaller business so we can't go crazy. As for timeline, we'd love to have something live within the next month or so since we're trying to grow before the busy season hits.
One last thing: do you have a domain name and hosting already set up, or will those need to be purchased as part of this project?

We don't have anything set up yet—we'd need you to handle all of that. We have a business name picked out, so we're hoping the domain is still available, but I'm not sure how that works or what it costs.

[DONE]

**Summary of Requirements Gathered:**

- **Business:** Local home cleaning service targeting busy homeowners in the area who prefer to outsource cleaning
- **Current marketing:** Word-of-mouth and neighborhood Facebook groups; looking to expand reach
- **Website goal:** Lead generation via a contact/quote request form (capturing home details and cleaning needs) plus a visible phone number for calls
- **Branding assets:** Existing logo and color scheme from Facebook page; has phone photos of past jobs (before/afters) that may need organizing; open to new professional photography
- **Marketing strategy:** Priority on local SEO/Google visibility (e.g., "cleaning service near me" searches) and Google Business presence; interest in Facebook/Instagram ads; not pursuing email marketing at this time
- **Budget:** $2,000–$5,000 total for website + marketing setup
- **Timeline:** Live within ~1 month, ahead of busy season
- **Domain/Hosting:** None set up yet; business name is chosen but domain availability unknown; needs full setup handled
I want to create an online store for handmade jewelry. I need product pages, a shopping cart, and something for payments. I'd like it to look clean and modern.
What's your estimated total number of products you'll be selling, and do you plan to offer variations per product (e.g., different sizes, metals, or gemstone colors) that customers can choose from?

I'm starting with around 50-75 pieces, but I plan to grow that over time. And yes, definitely — most of my jewelry comes in different sizes, and a lot of pieces have options like metal type (silver, gold, rose gold) or gemstone colors, so customers need to be able to pick those when they order.
Which payment methods do you want to support (e.g., credit/debit cards, PayPal, Apple/Google Pay), and do you have a preferred payment processor like Stripe or PayPal already in mind?

I'd definitely want credit and debit cards at minimum since that's what most people use. PayPal would be nice too since a lot of my customers probably have that. I haven't really looked into payment processors yet — I've heard Stripe mentioned a lot, so that seems like a safe bet, but I'm open to whatever works best.
Since each piece can have limited stock (e.g., only a few in a certain size/metal combo), do you need real-time inventory tracking that automatically marks variants as "sold out" once they run out?

Yeah, that's important to me — I don't want customers ordering something that's already sold out. I make these pieces myself, so inventory changes fairly often. Real-time tracking would definitely help avoid the headache of having to manually update things or deal with overselling.

Do you need a full admin dashboard where you can log in to add/edit products, update inventory, and view/manage orders yourself, or would you prefer a simpler setup where a developer handles product updates for you initially?

I'd definitely want to manage it myself — I'll be adding new pieces regularly and updating inventory as I make things, so I can't rely on a developer to do that every time. An admin dashboard where I can log in and handle products and orders would be essential for me.
Do you need built-in shipping options (e.g., calculated shipping rates, flat rate, or free shipping thresholds) and will you be shipping only domestically or internationally as well?

I'll be shipping domestically for now, so I'm thinking flat rate shipping to keep it simple. Maybe eventually I'll add international shipping, but let's start with just the US. I don't think I need super complex shipping calculations — just a straightforward flat fee would work for me.
Do you have a target launch timeframe or budget range in mind for this project?

I'm hoping to get it up and running within the next 2-3 months since I want to start selling online soon. As for budget, I'm not entirely sure what's realistic, but I'm looking to keep costs reasonable — maybe somewhere in the low thousands? I'm willing to invest to do it right, but I also don't want to overspend on features I don't actually need yet.

[DONE]

**Summary of Requirements Gathered:**

- **Project:** Online store for handmade jewelry, with a clean, modern design
- **Product Catalog:** 50–75 pieces at launch, expected to grow over time
- **Product Variations:** Size, metal type (silver/gold/rose gold), and gemstone color options per product
- **Core Features:** Product pages, shopping cart, checkout/payments
- **Payments:** Credit/debit cards and PayPal support, using Stripe as the likely processor
- **Inventory:** Real-time tracking with automatic "sold out" status per variant to prevent overselling
- **Admin Access:** Full self-service dashboard for managing products, inventory, and orders (no developer dependency)
- **Shipping:** Domestic (US) only for now, flat-rate shipping; international shipping possible later
- **Timeline:** 2–3 months to launch
- **Budget:** Low thousands range, cost-conscious but open to investing in the right features
I'm building a SaaS tool for small accounting firms. It should let them track client invoices, send reminders, and generate monthly reports. I want a subscription model.

What are the different types of users who will access this tool, and what distinct permissions or capabilities should each role have (e.g., firm owner/admin, staff accountant, and possibly the firm's clients themselves)?

Good question. I see three main user types:

**Firm owners/admins** would need full access — they'd manage team members, set up client accounts, view all invoices and reports, and handle billing.

**Staff accountants** would create and send invoices, track payments, and generate reports for their clients, but shouldn't access firm-level settings or billing.

**Clients** — yeah, I think they should be able to view their own invoices and payment status, maybe get notified about overdue amounts, but that's it. They shouldn't see other clients' data or anything about the firm's operations.

For invoicing, do you need firms to manually create/enter invoices within your tool, or should it integrate with existing accounting software (like QuickBooks, Xero) to pull invoice data automatically? And separately, do you need actual payment processing (clients paying through the platform via Stripe/etc.), or is this just for tracking and reminders while payment happens elsewhere?

Good points. For the invoicing — I think most of my target users already use QuickBooks or Xero, so integrating with those would be a huge win. Manually entering invoices seems tedious and error-prone. That's definitely something they'd want.

As for payment processing, honestly, I'm not sure if we need to handle that directly. I think the priority is tracking and sending reminders. If clients can click a link and pay through Stripe or something similar, that's fine — we don't necessarily need to own the whole payment flow. Keep it simple for now.

For the automated reminders, what triggers should control when they're sent (e.g., X days before due date, on the due date, X days after becoming overdue), and should firms be able to customize the reminder schedule and message templates themselves, or will you provide fixed defaults?

I'd want reminders to go out a few days before the due date — maybe 5 days — then on the due date itself, and then again if it's overdue, like 10 days past due. That covers the main touchpoints.

Definitely, firms should be able to customize this though. Different firms might have different policies, and they'd want their own branding and tone in the messages. So yeah, they should be able to adjust the timing and edit templates themselves. But I'd provide solid defaults so they can just use it out of the box if they want.

For the subscription model itself, how do you envision pricing being structured — for example, tiered plans based on number of clients or team members, a flat rate per firm, or something else — and do you have a rough sense of how many tiers you'd want to offer?

I'm thinking tiered pricing makes the most sense. Something like a starter plan for solo practitioners or very small firms, a mid-tier for firms with maybe 5-10 team members and a bunch of clients, and then a higher tier for larger operations. Three tiers seems reasonable.

I'd probably base it on the number of team members rather than clients — that's easier for firms to understand and predict. Maybe $50, $150, and $300 a month or something like that? I haven't locked in exact numbers yet, but the idea is that it scales with their business size without being so expensive that small firms can't afford it.

That's a solid framework. Now let's talk about the monthly reports — what specific information should they contain (e.g., outstanding balances, payment history, overdue summaries, revenue trends), and do firms need to customize/brand these reports before sending them to clients or using them internally?

The reports should definitely show outstanding balances, what's been paid, and overdue summaries — those are the essentials. Revenue trends month-over-month would be useful too, so they can see if collections are improving or getting worse.

For customization, I think they'd want to brand it with their firm's logo and maybe customize which sections to include, but I don't think it needs to be super flexible. A solid template they can tweak a bit would probably be enough. They might send these to clients, but more importantly they're using them internally to understand their cash flow and follow up on problem accounts.

One last important question: do you have a target launch timeline or existing technical constraints (e.g., specific hosting preferences, need for mobile apps, or must integrate with a particular authentication system) that would shape how this gets built?

I'm hoping to launch something in the next 6-8 months, ideally. I want to get an MVP out relatively quickly so I can start talking to potential customers and getting feedback.

As for technical stuff, I don't have strong preferences there — that's more your call as the builder. A web app is the priority. Mobile would be nice down the road, but not essential for launch. And honestly, I'm not married to any specific authentication system. Whatever's easiest and most standard would work for me.

[DONE]

**Summary of Requirements Gathered:**

- **User Roles:**
  - Firm Owners/Admins: Full access — team management, client setup, all invoices/reports, billing
  - Staff Accountants: Create/send invoices, track payments, generate reports (no firm settings/billing access)
  - Clients: View-only access to their own invoices/payment status, receive overdue notifications

- **Invoicing:**
  - Integration with QuickBooks/Xero (no manual entry needed)
  - No in-app payment processing required — link out to Stripe or similar for actual payment collection

- **Reminders:**
  - Automated triggers: 5 days before due, on due date, 10 days overdue
  - Firms can customize timing and message templates/branding
  - Solid default templates provided out of the box

- **Subscription Model:**
  - Tiered pricing (3 tiers) based on number of team members
  - Rough pricing: ~$50 / $150 / $300 per month (Starter, Mid, Large)

- **Reports:**
  - Monthly reports include: outstanding balances, payments received, overdue summaries, revenue trends (MoM)
  - Firms can add branding/logo and toggle sections; used both internally and optionally shared with clients

- **Timeline & Technical Constraints:**
  - Target launch: 6–8 months, MVP-first approach
  - Web app priority; mobile app is a future consideration
  - No strong preferences on hosting or auth — open to standard/best-practice recommendations
I need a website for my restaurant in Paris. It should show the menu, allow table reservations, and have a contact page. We post a lot on Instagram so maybe something for that too.

Great, thanks for the overview! Let's dig into the details.

What are the must-have details on the menu page — do you need it organized by categories (starters, mains, desserts, drinks), with prices, photos, and dietary/allergen info, or would a simple PDF menu upload be enough?

Categories and prices are definitely important — our menu changes seasonally, so being able to update it easily matters. Photos would be nice too, since food looks so much better that way. We probably don't need to go crazy with allergen info right now, but it would be good to have room for that eventually since a few customers ask about it.

Perfect, that gives me a clear picture for the menu. Now let's talk about reservations — do you want the booking system to just collect requests (name, date, time, party size) that you confirm manually via email/phone, or do you need real-time table availability with instant confirmation (possibly integrating with a service like OpenTable or Resy)?

Honestly, we'd prefer to confirm manually — we like talking to customers anyway, and our seating is pretty flexible depending on the day. Real-time availability sounds complicated and expensive. So just collecting their info and us following up would work perfectly fine.

Got it — a simple reservation request form it is. For the Instagram piece, are you picturing a live feed of your latest posts embedded on the site (updating automatically), or just a link/icon that sends visitors to your Instagram profile?

A live feed would be really cool — it keeps the site fresh without us having to manually update it. We post pretty regularly, so it would be nice to show that off automatically rather than just linking away.

That makes sense for keeping the site lively. Since your menu changes seasonally, will you or your staff need to update the menu yourselves through an easy admin dashboard (no coding), or are you comfortable relying on a developer each time changes are needed?

We'd definitely need to update it ourselves — we change things fairly often and I don't want to wait around for a developer every time. So yeah, an easy admin area where I can just add or edit dishes and prices would be essential.
Good to know — a self-service admin panel it is. Since you're in Paris, should the website be in French only, or do you need both French and English (or other languages) for international visitors?
French and English would be good — we get a lot of tourists, especially English speakers, so having both languages makes sense. Just those two though, I think that covers our customers.

Perfect, French and English it is. Last question: for the contact page, do you want it to include just an address, phone number, and email, or also things like an embedded Google Map, opening hours, and social media icons?

A map would be helpful since people coming from out of town might need directions. Opening hours definitely — we're closed Mondays and Tuesdays so that's important to show. And yeah, social media icons make sense since we're active on Instagram anyway. Phone and email too, of course.

[DONE]

**Project Summary: Restaurant Website (Paris)**

- **Menu Page**: Organized by categories (starters, mains, desserts, drinks), with prices and photos; seasonal updates via self-service admin panel; structure should allow future addition of allergen/dietary info
- **Reservations**: Simple request form (name, date, time, party size) — manually confirmed by staff via phone/email; no real-time availability or third-party booking integration needed
- **Instagram Integration**: Live embedded feed showing latest posts automatically, updating without manual effort
- **Admin/CMS**: Easy-to-use, no-code admin dashboard for restaurant staff to add/edit menu items and prices independently
- **Languages**: Bilingual site — French and English (to accommodate tourists)
- **Contact Page**: Address with embedded Google Map, phone number, email, opening hours (closed Mondays & Tuesdays), and social media icons
I want to run a digital marketing campaign for my new fitness app. The target is people aged 25–40 who like running. I want to use Instagram and Google Ads.

What is the primary goal of this campaign — app downloads, sign-ups/trials, brand awareness, or something else — and do you have a specific, measurable target (e.g., number of installs or a cost-per-install goal)?

My main goal is definitely to get downloads and sign-ups for the app—I need people actually trying it out.
